proposal.title: Engagement Proposal — Rapid Organisational Diagnostic
proposal.body:
PROPOSAL — RAPID ORGANISATIONAL DIAGNOSTIC
For: {{ORG}} · Attn: {{CONTACT}} · Date: {{DATE}}
From: Rahul K. Vimal — OD Consultant & C4D Practitioner, Delhi

1 · WHAT YOU TOLD ME
[Write their problem in THEIR OWN WORDS from the call. Quote them. Do not
paraphrase into consultant language.]

2 · WHAT I WILL DO
A diagnosis before any solution: interviews with board, staff and field
(6–8 people), review of your documents (policies, reports, formats), and
direct observation of how work actually moves. I look before I fix.

3 · WHAT YOU RECEIVE
· A scored organisational capacity baseline (my assessment instrument,
  four domains — your starting point, measured, not guessed)
· A written diagnostic report in plain language your team can read
· A feedback session with leadership: findings first, priorities agreed together
· An action plan — a small number of changes your team can realistically
  adopt, with measurable indicators

4 · WHAT I NEED FROM YOU
One focal point for scheduling · honest access to people and documents ·
leadership present at the feedback session · an owner named for each change.

5 · TIMELINE
2–3 weeks from start date.

6 · INVESTMENT
Pilot rate: ₹45,000 (standard rate for this diagnostic: ₹75,000–1,20,000).
I am building documented case evidence in this sector, so my first five
engagements run at this pilot rate. In exchange I ask for a written case
study and a reference I can name. This rate applies to the first five
engagements only and expires by design.

7 · PAYMENT
50% (₹22,500) to begin · 50% at handover, when your named owners hold the
deliverables and the review calendar is set.

[IF FCRA-FUNDED, add only this line: "Happy to align the contract
structure with your FCRA auditor's guidance." Nothing further.]

Valid 14 days. To proceed, reply confirming and I will send the Terms of
Reference for signature.

Rahul K. Vimal · rkv.consults@gmail.com · +91 9953724719

tor.title: Terms of Reference — OD Engagement
tor.body:
TERMS OF REFERENCE
Between: {{ORG}} ("the Organisation") and Rahul K. Vimal, OD Consultant
("the Consultant") · Date: {{DATE}}

1 · SCOPE
IN: organisational diagnosis (interviews, document review, observation),
scored capacity baseline, diagnostic report, feedback session, action plan.
OUT: implementation of changes, fundraising, legal/financial advice,
anything not written here. Additions are agreed in writing as new scope.

2 · DELIVERABLES & TIMELINE
Capacity baseline + diagnostic report + feedback session + action plan,
within [X] weeks of the start date below.

3 · THE ORGANISATION PROVIDES
A named focal point · access to staff for interviews (confidential; see 6)
· documents on request · leadership at the feedback session · a named owner
per agreed change. If access stops, the timeline pauses; two weeks of
blocked access and either party may close the engagement per clause 8.

4 · FEES & PAYMENT
Total: ₹45,000 (pilot rate, first-five engagements).
50% on signing (work begins on receipt) · 50% at handover — defined as the
deliverables transferred to named owners with a review calendar set. Not
tied to report delivery; tied to handover.

5 · CASE STUDY & REFERENCE (the pilot-rate exchange)
The Organisation agrees to: (a) a written case study naming the
Organisation, describing the engagement and its outcomes, reviewed and
approved by the Organisation before any use; (b) serving as a nameable
reference. Financial figures appear only with separate written consent.

6 · CONFIDENTIALITY
Both ways. The Organisation's internal information stays internal. Staff
interview content is never attributed to a named person without that
person's permission. The Consultant's templates and methods remain the
Consultant's.

7 · MATERIALS
Deliverables belong to the Organisation. The Consultant's underlying
templates, instruments and methods remain the Consultant's and may be
reused elsewhere without the Organisation's data.

8 · CLOSING EARLY
Either party, 7 days' written notice. Fees settle pro-rata against
delivered work.

Signed:
For {{ORG}}: ____________________  Date: ______
Rahul K. Vimal: ____________________  Date: ______

interview-guide.title: Diagnosis Interview Guide (Step 8)
interview-guide.body:
DIAGNOSIS INTERVIEWS — GUIDE
45 minutes each · 6–8 people across board / office / field · notes by hand.

SAY FIRST, EVERY TIME:
"I'm trying to understand how work actually moves here — not to judge
anyone. Nothing you say will be quoted with your name without your
permission. The report describes patterns, not people."

THE QUESTIONS (in order; skip what the role makes irrelevant):
1 · Walk me through yesterday, start to finish.
2 · When [the issue from intake] happens, what do you do, step by step?
3 · How does information reach you — and how do you pass it on?
4 · What happens to your work when you're away for a week?
5 · What did this organisation START doing in the last year, and who made
    that happen?  (self-initiated change = adoption capacity)
6 · What tools/registers/formats were started and then stopped? Why?
    (the graveyard — if there are three, format quality is not the problem)
7 · Where does work pile up or stall? Show me if you can.
8 · Who decides [X]? Who do you actually ask when stuck?
9 · Which meeting matters most here? What would break if it stopped?
10 · What does the funder ask for that is hardest to produce?
11 · If you had one free week to fix one thing here, what?
12 · If the founder/director were unreachable for two weeks, what happens?

CLOSE: "What should I have asked that I didn't?"

OBSERVE while on site (don't ask, watch): where records physically live ·
who interrupts whom · what's on the walls · which registers look used vs
decorative · language each document lives in vs language people work in.

AFTER EACH INTERVIEW, note immediately: 3 facts · 1 surprise · 1 pattern
forming · evidence seen (not just claims heard).

capacity-assessment.title: Organisational Capacity Assessment (scored baseline)
capacity-assessment.body:
CAPACITY ASSESSMENT — SCORED BASELINE
Adapted for small Indian NGOs (5–30 staff) from the Marguerite Casey OCAT
lineage. Scored BY THE CONSULTANT from evidence (interviews, documents,
observation) — never self-scored, never from opinion.

SCALE, per item: 1 = absent · 2 = informal/person-dependent ·
3 = written but unevenly used · 4 = systematic and used. Note the EVIDENCE
beside every score. No evidence = score 1, flag it.

A · LEADERSHIP & GOVERNANCE
A1 Board meets and minutes its meetings
A2 Decisions get recorded and communicated, not just made
A3 A second line exists — someone besides the founder can run things
A4 Staff can state what the organisation is trying to achieve this year
A5 Succession/absence: founder away two weeks, work continues

B · MANAGEMENT & OPERATIONS
B1 Roles written; people know who does what
B2 Work is measured by output/result, not attendance/task
B3 The recurring meeting is goal-driven with follow-ups tracked
B4 Task-loads realistic — no chronic single-person overload
B5 Knowledge survives exits — a leaver's work is recoverable

C · SYSTEMS & COMPLIANCE
C1 Core policies exist AND staff can say what's in them
C2 Books monthly, not audit-time; audit filed on time
C3 Statutory current (12A/80G/FCRA-as-applicable/POSH if 10+)
C4 Standard formats: report, budget, proposal — not built fresh each time
C5 A record from last year findable in under ten minutes

D · COMMUNICATION & DELIVERY
D1 Field information reaches the office intact and on time
D2 Funder reporting produced without crisis
D3 Documentation is a habit (a standing agenda item), not an event
D4 Staff have a real channel to raise issues — and use it
D5 External presence (site/social) reflects actual current work

SCORING: 20 items × 1–4 = 20–80.
20–35 FOUNDATIONAL — person-dependent; build the basics first
36–59 EMERGING — pieces exist, no coherent whole; standardise + embed
60–80 SYSTEMATIC — polish, succession and scale questions

Re-run the same instrument at engagement end (Step 12) and at +90 days.
Baseline → endline movement, per item, IS the case study evidence.
